output.brief: The rise from 0.31% to 0.41% looks like ordinary week-to-week variation. Over the previous 26 weeks the rate averaged 0.354%, and the policy's upper limit for a normal week is 0.482%. Last week's 0.411% is inside that. Three earlier weeks were higher and were investigated with no fault found. The error-budget burn was 0.82x, well under the 2x paging threshold. The dashboard count matches a recount from the raw logs. Booking completion and support complaints did not change. The v4.18 pods did error more during the rollout. But the last five rollouts, including a config-only redeploy of the unchanged v4.16 image, all showed the same gap. It comes from new pods starting with a cold cache, and it adds only 10–20 errors per rollout. That is far too few to explain the roughly 2,000 extra errors in the week. I am fairly sure of this, though I did not rule out the replica move or partner-sync traffic as small contributors. Next steps: don't roll back, note the week at ops review, keep all alerting on, and apply the standard check to the coming week. Do not mute the burn-rate page. Revisit only if the next week goes above the band.
